answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed if the agent is caught operating duplicate identities. A sybil cluster must sink real capital into every fake persona, and each bond sits at risk until the cluster reaches its nadir—total loss—so cheap mass registration dies. Think of a pearl: each identity must coat a real irritant with costly nacre over time, not spray pigment on sand. Duplicates cannot amortize that cost across many masks.
